cases.input: Create an internal job description, executive-search brief and public posting from an approved role architecture without changing the role itself.
requiredBehaviors: create three audience-specific projections of the same normative role
trace every hard requirement to the role architecture
keep candidate assessment anchored to role architecture rather than public copy
forbiddenBehaviors: invent new must-have criteria for marketing appeal
change decision rights or scope while drafting copy

cases.input: The internal role architecture contains sensitive turnaround context that should not be disclosed in the public posting.
requiredBehaviors: preserve the underlying role semantics
abstract confidential context appropriately in public copy
record the difference as a communication decision rather than a role change
forbiddenBehaviors: delete the underlying success requirement from the normative role

cases.input: A corporate executive-role template includes an organigram, reporting table, proprietary footer, placeholders for headcount budget travel and hybrid model, and older requirement wording. Current approved role evidence already confirms reporting, travel and hybrid details but not headcount or budget.
requiredBehaviors: inherit the corporate document structure labels and visual context where useful
replace travel and hybrid placeholders with confirmed values
leave genuinely unknown headcount and budget open or remove unnecessary placeholders without inventing values
validate all inherited requirement wording against the current role architecture and scorecard
forbiddenBehaviors: copy historical requirements merely because they are in the corporate template
retain placeholders for facts already confirmed

cases.input: The executive-search brief correctly treats direct industry experience and two regulatory regimes as hard requirements, but an older public posting says the industry is only preferred and allows a broader adjacent sector.
requiredBehaviors: keep the hard requirement semantically hard across the public projection
remove the unsupported broader alternative rather than averaging the two versions
allow the public posting to be shorter without contradicting the normative role
forbiddenBehaviors: downgrade a must-have to preferred for candidate appeal
treat the legacy public wording as equally normative
silently broaden the eligible candidate pool beyond the role architecture

cases.input: Create German and English public postings plus an English search brief from the same approved role. The German draft says very good German and excellent English, while the English legacy copy says excellent command of both languages.
requiredBehaviors: resolve language requirements from the normative role rather than preserve translation drift
make all language versions semantically equivalent on must-have versus preferred criteria
check reporting scope location travel and experience thresholds across languages
forbiddenBehaviors: allow one language version to tighten or weaken a requirement
treat translation as permission to change normative meaning

cases.input: A long executive-search package repeats transformation, regulatory depth, leadership and product understanding in the mandate, responsibilities, special-position section, requirements and search guidance.
requiredBehaviors: consolidate each concept into one primary explanatory section
use search guidance to operationalise requirements through evidence red flags and interview questions rather than restating them
retain repetition only when the semantic function changes
forbiddenBehaviors: repeat the same requirement verbatim across several sections
remove needed evidence or interview operationalisation in the name of brevity

cases.input: Make the posting more selective by adding elite university, exact age range and a specific prior title that are absent from the role architecture.
requiredBehaviors: reject unsupported selection criteria
retain only role-related capability and outcome requirements
route genuine role changes back to role-architecture
forbiddenBehaviors: add unsupported prestige or personal filters
silently modify the normative role while authoring
